label: paragraph_title
text: COUNTY RESULTS.

label: text
text: Local. cricket enthusiasts who remember Captain F. Havelock Davies, R.A. and Midahipman (afterwards Sub-Lieut.) Evans, R.N., will be pleased to hear of their progress in the game at Home. Last season Captain Davies played in representative matches at Home. This season he was in the Army team which beat Oxford University in rather starthing fashion and the former Hongkong airport fast bowler took the most wickets. He also played in the Army v. Navy match on July 14.

label: text
text: Lieut. Evans was a bowler for the Navy and he was also honoured in the same match at Lord's going in last to but for the senior service. It is rather a coincidence that two former Hongkong players should be on opposing side in the best company at Home.

label: text
text: Captain Olliver, who with Captain Davies, made a name in Hong Kong cricket, has also been doing well.

label: text
text: Eient. Evans is a nephew of W. H. B. Evans, the famous Hompshir's cricketer of former days.

label: paragraph_title
text: YORKSHIRE CHAMPIONS?

label: text
text: On Saturday the Surrey v. Yorkshire match commenced at the Oval. After this Surrey have to play Middlesex at Lord's. The champions' remaining fixtures are v. Sussex at Brighton and Y. Somerset at Taunton. Even if Surrey were to win at the Oval it is difficult to see the championship taken from Yorkshire. However, Surrey now have a good chance to remain in the second position as Tannashire have dropped more points—as will be seen in the results below. The table is posted up to date.

text: CANTON EMBARGO.

label: text
text: SERIOUSNESS FELT IN LONDON.

label: text
text: MINISTER TO RETURN?

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: The "Daily Mail" states that the seriousness of the crisis between Canton and Hongkong is revealed by messages reaching the London headquarters of firms trading in the Far East, appealing for representations to be made to the British Government not to delay definition and suggesting the immediate despatch to Peking of an eminent person duthorised to negotiate an agreement.

label: text
text: The messages allude to the unfortunate absence from Peking of the British Minister, Sir Ronald Mucley, who is on sick leave in England.

label: text
text: The "Daily Mail" learns that Sir Ronald hopes to have recovered sufficiently to enable him to return to Peking in about three weeks.

label: text
text: CANADA'S REQUEST.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Rcuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: The Merchants' Exchange has telegraphed to Mr. Mackenzie King requesting him to advise the British Government of the "inevitable and very serious effect on Canadian export; shipping and trade in the Far East of the Chinese boycott on British goods and shipping.

label: text
text: Chinese firms are demanding the emotion of Canadian labels and marks of identification and the consignment of goods on United States ships for the purpose of making the population believe they are of America's origin.

label: paragraph_title
text: FLIGHT TO POLE.

label: text
text: AMUNDSEN AND GERMAN PLANS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, August 22.

label: text
text: Evidence that the victory of the North Pole over Captain Amundsen has not deterred the explorer in his determination to reach the Pole by air is contained in a message from Oslo, which declares that Captain Amundsen and Lieutenant Riiser Larsen have gone to Hamburg, en route to Italy, to negotiate for the purchase of an airship for a 1926 polar expedition.

label: text
text: It is announced that prominent Germans, including professors, bankers and authors have signed an appeal for subscriptions to enable Captain Eckener, who piloted the ZR3 to America to build a Zeppelin for Arctic exploration.

label: paragraph_title
text: GERMANS ABROAD.

label: text
text: BRITISH EMPIRE TO LIFT RESTRICTIONS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Berlin, August 22.

label: text
text: In official quarters it is expected that the restrictions preventing Germans from taking up their domiciles in foreign colonies, particularly the British Dominions, will be abolished within eight months. It is stated that the restrictions have been already removed in respect of Ceylon, Tanganyika and South West Africa, while Australia and New Zealand will follow suit at the end of the year.

label: paragraph_title
text: REDS TO GO.

label: text
text: SHANGHAI MEN ATTACK BOLSHEVIKS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, August 22.

label: text
text: Ill-feeling against the Bolshevik section of local labour leaders culminated this evening in an attack on the headquarters of the Shanghai Labour Association in the Chinese city by a large crowd of strikers, armed with miscellaneous weapons, including sticks, and knives.

label: text
text: Both sides had casualties and it is reported that one or two Reds were killed.

label: text
text: The demonstrators complained that they had been deceived and robbed by the Bolsheviks.

label: text
text: ATTEMPT ON FRENCH GOVERNOR.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Port de France (Martinique),
August 22.

label: text
text: Miscreants to-day fired on the Governor, when he was boarding a steamer. He is seriously injured.

label: text
text: The name of the chief assailant of the Governor is given as Richard who is said to be the son of a Councillor General who was killed during the electoral disorders last May.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOUTH AFRICA POLICE REPUISED.

label: text
text: Cape Town, August 22.

label: text
text: At Elisabethville a native religious fanatic and a number of followers, in attempting to make forcible conversions in the Samantha district, are reported to have slaughtered 50 natives in one village alone. A patrol of native police sent to investigate were driven off, losing a number killed and wounded.

label: text
text: The Belgian authorities have despatched troops from Elisabeth-ville to the scene.
